archetypes.name: quiet-init-purity
archetypes.rationale: The plan introduces a lib that must have zero raw >&2 writes so it is safe to source from quiet-init callers, but the same lib contains emit_failed_agent_stderr_tail_raw which does emit to FD 2 — verify that the plan's caller segregation (non-quiet run-external-agent.sh vs quiet-init collect-agent-results.sh / launch-claude-review.sh) is airtight and that no code path lets a quiet-init caller inadvertently invoke the raw emitter.
archetypes.prompt_body: Audit whether the plan's 'no raw >&2 in the lib' invariant is structurally enforced or only relies on caller discipline. Check that every function in lib-failed-agent-stderr-tail.sh is categorized as either (a) pure stdout/file, safe for quiet-init callers, or (b) raw >&2, restricted to non-quiet callers — and that emit_failed_agent_stderr_tail_raw falls strictly in category (b). Verify that collect-agent-results.sh and launch-claude-review.sh use only larch_err (quiet-safe) and never call the raw emitter. Check whether sourcing the lib file itself (outside any function call) could trigger any side effects that violate quiet-init. Also confirm the plan does not require adding the lib source to any quiet-init preamble in a way that breaks the lint-no-raw-stderr-after-quiet-init check. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: fd-routing-integrity
archetypes.rationale: The plan's correctness depends on the tail output never contaminating the stdout KV plane that collect-agent-results.sh parses; multiple code paths converge on FD 2 but the plan's fenced block format and larch_err line-by-line emission are distinct and may interact unexpectedly with downstream parsers.
archetypes.prompt_body: Verify that every surfacing path for the stderr tail (emit_failed_agent_stderr_tail_raw via raw >&2, dedup-emit pass via larch_err line-by-line, and the fenced block header/footer) is provably FD-2-only and structurally cannot appear on stdout. Check whether the plan's 'line-by-line larch_err' strategy for the fenced block body produces valid output or whether larch_err adds prefixes/timestamps that would corrupt the fence structure the operator sees. Confirm that the plan's harness assertion 'stdout RESULTS lines are unchanged when a .stderr-tail exists' is actually specified in the test extensions and covers the collector's stdout KV contract byte-by-byte. Assess whether the existing full-stderr re-emit in launch-claude-review.sh (lines ~173-178) and the new .stderr-tail dedup path can both fire for the same failure, producing double output to chat, and whether the plan explicitly handles or accepts that. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: sidecar-lifecycle
archetypes.rationale: The .stderr-tail sidecar is created by run-external-agent.sh or launch-claude-review.sh and later read by collect-agent-results.sh in a separate process; the plan's timing assumptions about when the sidecar exists relative to the collector's dedup pass and tmpdir cleanup need explicit verification against the existing done-sentinel handoff contract.
archetypes.prompt_body: Trace the lifecycle of the .stderr-tail sidecar: it is written by run-external-agent.sh (foreground) or launch-claude-review.sh (background launcher), then read by the collector's dedup pass after the retry loop settles. Check whether the plan guarantees the sidecar is present before the collector's dedup pass reads it — specifically whether the .done sentinel that signals slot completion is written after or before .stderr-tail, and whether a race can cause the collector to see a missing sidecar for a genuinely failed slot. Verify the plan's claim that .stderr-tail is 'intentionally NOT added to design-log-publish.sh's exclusion glob' is consistent with the existing exclusion logic in design-log-publish.sh and will not be swept by a wildcard pattern that already covers .stderr-tail. Check whether the sidecar's atomic write (mktemp + mv) is correctly sequenced relative to tmpdir cleanup on both the success and failure paths, so that a late-arriving success does not leave orphaned .stderr-tail files. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.
